A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Random Feature Representation Boosting and contain complete, readable main texts and Appendices A–E. Text, equations, tables and figures support a reliable comparison, including material relocated within the appendices.

before.justification: v2 reports original OpenML regression and classification experiments, synthetic point-cloud separation results, initialization ablations and larger-scale evaluations in Section 4 and Appendix E.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments, including measured predictive performance and training times, and expands the numerical reporting in Tables 5–7.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.3 and Algorithms 1–2 retain the same random features, exact-greedy and gradient-greedy fitting procedures, normalization, line search and predictor updates. The revised conclusion describes the existing method more explicitly.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 91 OpenML tasks, concentric-circle separation task and four larger-scale datasets in Appendix E.5, including CoverType and YearPredictionMSD. No dataset, task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same comparator membership: RFNN, E2E MLP ResNet, ridge/logistic regression and, where applicable, XGBoost, alongside the same RFRBoost variants. The added related-work citation is not an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: The nested five-fold evaluation, 100 Optuna trials, OpenML sample cap, preprocessing and model settings remain unchanged. The point-cloud protocol and larger-scale splits, training sizes and hyperparameter grids also match.

E4.justification: The SWIM-versus-i.i.d. ablation in Appendix E.4, point-cloud case study and training-size analyses in Appendix E.5 retain the same questions and evidence. Relocated appendix displays do not introduce new analyses.

E5.justification: Tables 5–7 expand from mean-only entries to means with parenthesized apparent dispersion estimates throughout the main 91-dataset benchmark. This substantially extends dataset-level uncertainty reporting, although the statistic is not explicitly defined. Existing fold/run counts, significance tests and confidence-interval reporting elsewhere are unchanged; additional runs are not established.

E6.justification: New numerical entries accompany unchanged means: Table 5 reports RFRBoost on dataset 3 as 0.996 (0.002), previously 0.996; Table 7 reports Gradient RFRBoost on dataset 41021 as 0.231 (0.011), previously 0.231. All 557 mean-score entries, highlighted winners and plotted findings are retained.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, formal results and derivations in Sections 2–3 and Appendices A–D are unchanged. Adding 'Problems' to Appendix A's heading does not revise its mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the same novelty, convex-fitting, theoretical and empirical claims. The conclusion's more explicit description of residual blocks approximating negative functional gradients restates the earlier account without broadening the claims.

C2.justification: The conclusion restates the existing distinction between optimizing representations and optimizing network weights. Interpretations of the benchmark results, SWIM tradeoffs, larger-data limitations and proposed fine-tuning application remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The implementation descriptions, NumPy snippets, SWIM sampling instructions, hyperparameter tables, hardware information and code-access statement are retained. No additional implementation or reproducibility information is disclosed.

R1.justification: Section 1.2 and the references add Biagini, Gonon and Walter (2024), 'Universal randomised signatures for generative time series modelling,' to the existing discussion of related random-feature approaches. The broader research positioning is unchanged.

P1.justification: The conclusion receives localized explanatory rewriting; Section 2.2 changes 'label space' to 'target space.' Appendix A's heading and acknowledgements are updated, and the generic Impact Statement is removed. The overall narrative and section organization remain stable.

P2.justification: Tables 5–7 are reformatted to accommodate parenthesized values, with smaller text in Table 7. Appendix displays reflow: Figures 5–6 move before Table 7, and Table 9 moves earlier. All ten figures retain identical image content.

improvement.justification: The added apparent dispersion estimates in Tables 5–7 supplement previously mean-only benchmark reporting, and the conclusion explains the method more clearly. These limited gains are tempered by the failure to define the parenthesized statistic and the smaller regression-table text. The methods, theory and central empirical findings remain unchanged.
